turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno

Your Honors, with due respect, none of the grounds raised by the respondent justifies the wholesale rejection of the prosecution's request for admission.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: The respondent argues that Rule 26 is inapplicable because impeachment proceedings are penal in character. But an impeachment trial, Your Honors, is neither an ordinary civil action nor a criminal prosecution. It is, as we have repeatedly said, a sui generis constitutional proceeding governed principally by the rules of the Senate sitting as an impeachment court. Where those rules do not specifically provide otherwise, the rules of court may be applied suppletorily. Subject always to the control and discretion of this Court. Hindi po criminal case ang impeachment trial at malinaw po sa Senate rules na dapat gamitin ang Rules of Court in a suppletory character. Kasama po sa Rules of Court ang request for admission kaya hindi sapat na sabihin penal in character ang impeachment upang tuluyang ipagbawal ito. The request for admission is not being invoked to alter the burden of proof or to compel the respondent to establish the prosecution's case and will not have that effect. Its purpose is simply to narrow the issues and avoid the needless presentation of witnesses and evidence on matters that are not genuinely disputed. Ang mga bank records na tinukoy po namin sa request for admission ay galing mismo sa mga bangko at idinerecho sa hukumang ito. Hindi po ito dumaan sa kamay ng prosekyusyon. To be clear, the respondent has not made any claim that they are fake or fabricated. Ang nagsubmit nitong records ay hindi po mga pipitsugin na bangko. These are known banks who would not submit fake documents to this court. They know how important this case is. They know the whole nation is watching. Nakataya ang kanilang pangalan at reputasyon dito. That is why we are saying that the authenticity of the bank documents is not genuinely disputed. Second, the request does not violate the respondent's rights against self-incrimination. It does not require her to take the witness stand, give an oral confession, or create evidence that is not already available to the parties and to this court. More importantly, most of the requested matters concern only the existence and authenticity of documents already produced by independent banks in compliance with the order or subpoena issued by this court. Indeed, the request merely seeks recognition of existing records, does not compel the respondent to generate new testimonial or documentary evidence against herself. The respondent relies on authorities involving an accused in a criminal prosecution. These rulings, we submit, should not be mechanically extended to this sui generis proceeding, particularly with respect to neutral and disputable matters that do not, by themselves, establish liability or culpability. Wala pong paglabag sa karapatan ng respondent laban sa self-incrimination, Your Honest Peace. Hindi po namin siya pinapaamin sa anumang kasalanan o pananagutan. Ang hinihingi lang po namin ay ang pagkilala sa mga dokumentong sinabmit mismo ng mga bangko pursuant to the subpoenas of this Court. Sa mga bagay na hindi naman tunay na pinagtatalo namin. Third, the request does not shift the burden of proof. An admission merely dispenses with proof of a matter that is no longer genuinely disputed. It has absolutely no effect on who has the burden of proof. Ang purpose lamang po ng aming request ay huwag ng pag-aksayahan ng oras ng hukuman ang mga bagay na hindi naman kailangan patunayan pa. Fourth, The marital and filial privileges cited by the respondent do not justify striking out the entire request. Those privileges generally concern the compelled testimony of one spouse against the other or of a person against a parent or child. Here, the prosecution is not compelling the respondent to testify against her spouse, parent or child. At most, any claim of privilege, if legitimate, should be considered in relation to the particular matter affected. It is not a basis for expunging the prosecution's request in its entirety. Hindi po nagiging privilege ang isang dokumento dahil lamang nabanggit dito ang asawang magulang o anak ng respondent. Hindi po natin pinipilit ang respondent na tumistigo sa kanya asawa. At kung meron mang particular na paksa na saklaw talaga ng privilege, iyon lamang ang dapat tukuyin at resolbahan. Hindi po dapat ibasura ang buong request for admission dahil lang doon. Fifth, the respondent's generalized objections based on relevance, remoteness, or the periods covered by the records cannot justify the wholesale rejection of the request. At the very least, this honorable court has already determined that there was sufficient basis to require the banks to produce these records through its compulsory process. Finally, the request is not a belated attempt to cure a deficiency in the prosecution's evidence. Again, the bank's records were produced during these proceedings pursuant to subpoenas. Once the records became available, the prosecution properly sought to narrow the issues surrounding them and avoid consuming the court's time by presenting numerous witnesses simply to establish matters that should not reasonably be disputed. Hindi po ito afterthought, Your Honors. Gaya ng nasabi ko kanina, inihain po ang request ng maging available ang mga dokumentong sinubmit ng mga bangko alinsunod sa SabPinas ng hukuman. Ang layunin po ay simple, tukuyin kung alin ang tunay na pinagtatalunan at huwag nang ubusin ang panahon at oras ng Korte sa pagpapatawag ng maraming witnesses para lamang patunayan ng mga bagay na hindi naman genuinely disputed. Your Honor, for these reasons, the prosecution respectfully submits that the objection should be overruled and that the matters covered by the request should be deemed admitted pursuant to Rule 26 of the Rules of Court. But, Your Honor, please, nevertheless, in the spirit of cooperation and to avoid unnecessary delay or disagreement, the prosecution has a proposal or proposition for the respondent. In their objection, the respondent claims And I quote, if indeed, this is from paragraph 41 for the record, quote, if indeed their intent was to shorten the proceedings, the prosecution has itself repeatedly utilized stipulations to dispense with the presentation of matters that are not genuinely disputed. If speed were truly the objective, the same course remained available. Since according to the respondent, the same course remains available, We are willing to enter into stipulations with the respondent in relation to the bank documents, as well as other documents produced by witnesses through the subpoenas issued by this court. These stipulations will be limited only to three basic matters. Number one, that the bank records exist. Number two, that they were produced by the identified banks pursuant to subpoenas issued by this honorable court. And number three, that they are genuine and authentic copies of the records maintained and produced by those banks. Ganun lang po kasimple, Your Honors. We will withdraw our request for admission if the respondent will agree to this. The proposed stipulations would not require the respondent to admit liability, the truth or accuracy of every entry, or the prosecution's interpretation of any transaction. The respondent would remain free to contest the relevance, meaning, Evidentiary weight and legal effect of the records. Kung makapagkasundoan po tayo to the defense, we would be able to dispense with about at least 10 to 20 witnesses who would be testifying on the same things anyway. Kung iaharap pa natin ng humigit-kumulang 20 karagdagan testigo para lang patunayan ng mga foundational matters na ito, malaking bahagi ng oras ng mga pagdinig ang masasayang. sa mga bagay na hindi naman tunay na pinagtatalo. In conclusion, Your Honor, the respondent herself expressly declared that stipulations remain available. The prosecution is prepared to take the respondent at her word. Therefore, we invite the respondent to engage in stipulations on these matters so that we can proceed with the actual litigation that must be done in this case. Maraming salamat po.

turns.text: Supreme Court decision. This is Pascual Jr. versus Board of Medical Examiners, which involves an administrative proceeding for future. And in this case, despite this being a mere administrative proceeding, the Court nonetheless upheld the right of the respondent to the absolute self-right against self-incrimination. In fact, and I will state the ruling of the court, the broad all-embracing sweep of the self-incrimination clause whenever appropriately invoked has been accorded due recognition by this court ever since the adoption of the Constitution. Bermudez versus Castillo. decided in 1937, ganun na po katagal ang garantiang ito, was quite categorical. As we there stated, this court is of the opinion that in order that the constitutional provision under consideration may prove to be a real protection and not a dead letter, it must be given a liberal and broad interpretation favorable to the person invoking it. The proceeding for forfeiture, while administrative in character, thus possesses a criminal or penal aspect. The case before us is not dissimilar. Petitioner would be similarly disadvantaged. He could suffer not the forfeiture of property, but the revocation of his license as a medical practitioner. For some, an even greater deprivation. The constitutional guarantee protects as well the right to silence. As far back as 1905, we had the occasion to declare, the accused has a perfect right to remain silent, and his silence cannot be used as a presumption of his guilt. Only last year in Chavez v. Court of Appeals speaking through Justice Sanchez, we reaffirmed the doctrine anew that it is the right of a defendant to forgo testimony. To remain silent unless he chooses to take the witness stand with undiluted, unfettered exercise of his own free, genuine will. Why it should be thus is not difficult to discern. The constitutional guarantee, along with other rights granted and accused, stands for a belief that while crime should not go unpunished and that the truth must be revealed, Such desirable objectives should not be accomplished according to means or methods offensive to the highest sense of respect accorded the human personality. More and more, in line with the democratic creed, the deference accorded an individual even though suspected of the most heinous crimes is given due weight. The quote from Chief Justice Warren, the Constitutional Foundation underlying the privilege is the respect of government. must accord to the dignity and integrity If the Supreme Court has applied the right against self-incrimination or the right to at least remain silent as far or as early as 1969 in a mere administrative proceeding because the proceeding as it had determined carries with it some penal sanction then all the more that this should be respected in an impeachment case regardless whether or not this is a Sui generis proceeding. Because the court had long recognized in INRE Corrileño that an impeachment trial is highly penal in character. turns.text: No personal knowledge po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sopena.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you. Before calling on Senator Joel Villanueva, may

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I ask Congressman Defensor, Congressman Barber, to kindly nudge Kong Benny a bit? It seems he's tired.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: He may want to rest somewhere but at least not right behind the witness.

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, I think he's praying for us.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I doubt that. He's

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: praying for the prosecution, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator-Judge, Joel Villanueva is recognized. You have two minutes. It's been a long day, I guess, because you just approved the budget last week. You may proceed when you're ready.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer, Mr. Senate President.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Mr. Witness, kayo na po, binanggit niyo, kahit na sa being lowest calculated and responsive bid or offer, hindi niyo po nakikita kung may competition ito, yung presyo, kung ilan niyong nagbibid. Tama po.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Correct po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: So, pwede niyo po bang sabihin sa amin, ilang beses po naging sole responsive bidder? O sole submitted quotation ang GenCorp?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: I have no record po or the full list po kung ilang beses po siyang nagiging.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: So wala po kayong record doon?

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Sa dami po ng awards, wala po kayong nakikita na ang PhilGEPS po paulit-ulit na GenCorp ang napipili ng parehong procuring entity? Office or end user? Para sa magkakatulad na produkto?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Naka-indicate po ito sa mga ina-upload na documents ng procuring entity. Pero as to the electronic data itself, sir, wala po. Kaya pag nagda-download kami, hindi po namin siya nakikita yung ganun pong information.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: So, pero Marlin, you would agree with me na repeated awards are not automatically unlawful?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: When it comes to legality, I am not really... Pero

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: yung frequency, product similarity, timing, competition are relevant to transparency and possible preferential patterns. In

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: my personal opinion, yes po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: So may red flags po ba ang PhilGEPS para makita na unusually repetitive awards o repository lang talaga po kayo?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Your Honor, actually we are currently developing those features bago pong dinidevelop namin na procuring system. So the current procuring system wala pa po. However, yung dinidevelop po namin ngayon kasama na po yung mga ganyang features, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: So gusto ko lang maintindihan, kung hindi po nagbe-verify ang PhilGEPS at wala rin pong naisasagawa na post-qualification or independent validation of ownership, beneficial ownership, at relationship declarations ng GenCorp, paano po nakakatiyak ang gobyerno na kumpleto, tama, at tunay po ang mga dokumentong isinusumite at walang direct or indirect personal... Familiar or financial or business relationship sa head of procuring entity ang sino mang opisyal o sangkot sa procurement?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Your Honor, siguro po. Yung upon approval po ng NGPA 12009, PSDBM po approved po ng budget for recreation of a new procurement system which align po sa 12009 which kasama po rito yung

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Detection po ng mga collusion and red tagging. And yung system po itself ngayon, the modernized PhilGepps, through the open data portal po, available po yung mga information publicly. And it can be viewed po ng kahit sino sa website po ng PhilGepps, included sa procurement dashboard. na mada-download po ng mga public yung aggregated data. Tapos, nandun din po sa procurement dashboard included and ine-enhance po namin yung beneficial owner's table. Meron po nung information for BO which kasama po sa mandate ng field job system under the 12009 and the open data portal po.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Yung mga enhancement po for the upcoming na bagong procurement system.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Ngunit sa ngayon,

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: tama

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: po bang sabihin sir na yung procurement records ay nagpapakita lamang ng mga deklarasyong isinusumite ng bidder, ngunit hindi po ito nagpapatunay na tama o kompleto ang mga deklarasyong ito?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Mga government agencies na ay gagamitin na po yung bagong itong isang modernized system natin, yung e-bidding po. So lahat po ng procurement would be through electronic na po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Sa darating na sistema.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Actually, we have po eh.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Kasi wala akong verification eh.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: We have the modernized PhilGEPS actually, sir. Yung 49 awarded contracts po kasi... were created and posted under the PhilGEPS 1.5. We are also maintaining the modernized PhilGEPS na ginagamit din po ng iba na nandun po yung e-bidding process. Ang e-bidding po, this will capture the end-to-end activity ng government agencies starting from the annual procurement plan up to the contract management. Some of the government agencies are utilizing it. Kagaya po ng Office of the President, ginagamit po nila yung e-bidding. Sir,

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: but with all due respect, but on this case, wala akong verification. Ang hirap po sabihin sa publiko na may maaasahan po kami na natukoy o maiwasan po yung anumang direct or indirect conflict of interest.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: With this case, I agree.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: That's so

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: unfortunate. Sir, last question ko na lang po. Susugan ko yung tinanong niya SP Win kanina. Doon po sa mga... Purchase request o award na binanggit niyo po yung mga small value awards dun sa GenCorp. May makikita po ba kayo dun na hinate sa magkakahiwalay na amounts o pag pinagsama nila ay maaaring lumampas doon sa applicable threshold yung ginawa po nila? May makikita po ba kayong ganun?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Meron po sa record dyan ang isang bid notice. May iba't ibang line item. However, iba-iba po yung category niya, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: I-clarify ko lang po yung question. Doon sa 15 na binanggit niyo po na small value procurements, ilan po yung magkakapareho o magkakalapit ang product description, end user, delivery period, at procurement date?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: For

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: the title itself po, Your Honor, same lang na catering services, food and catering services. Pero yung publish and award date naman po is iba-iba po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: And again, wala kayo nakikita dyan na hinate o magkakahiwalay yung amounts para lamang po lumampas dun sa... para hindi po... Masabi na lumampas dun sa applicable threshold. Just to see if there are...

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Based on the records ko lang. Wala naman po Your Honor

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Last na lang po. May ibidensya po ba sa PhilGeps na ang pagkakahati ay ginagawa upang umiwas po sa competitive bidding? Or wala po kayong sapat na record para sabihin po yun?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: The system po is designed so I think po... Hindi po inaalaw ng system pag may mga splitting na gano'n.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: So makikita niyo po?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Embedded sa system, hindi po aalaw pag gano'n.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Hindi iaalaw pagka ginawa po nila yun para lang umiwas dun po sa competitive bidding.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Salamat po for that clarification. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator-Judge, Ervin Tulfo is recognized. You may proceed, sir, when you're ready. You have two minutes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer. Gino'ng witness, nung nangyayari po itong Itong mga kontrata na ito. Wala ko kayo nakikitang problema? Kaya lumulusot po ito?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: During the process po ng bidding, hindi po kami visible or personally knowledgeable po. Kailan

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: nyo lang nalaman na may problema? Pinatawag na kayo sa Congress?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Yes, when we received po yung sabina.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: So, ibig sabihin kahit may glaring na...

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Nangyayari na hindi nasusunod ayon sa batas ang isang bidding, et cetera. Okay lang, lumulusot lang, lumulusot? Unless kung kayo ay... wala ba kayong kapangyarihan? Teka muna, questionin, teka muna, may problema ito, boss. Or tell your supervisor na may problema ho ito, boss. Ano ba ang nangyayari dito? Anong gagawin natin?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Your Honor, for our office po, kasi we are merely the repository of the data. So sa ongoing

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: ng kontrata, wala kayong alam? Tama

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: So ngayon na lang ninyo nalaman dahil may nagtanong na po, nagtanong na po ang House of Representatives, ang Committee on Justice, dalit sa impeachment?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Yes, po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: So ibig sabihin, Sir, meron ba kayang mga nangyayaring ikang anomalya na hindi nyo lang alam kasi repository lang kayo?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: For the oversight function po, it's not... The mandate po of the PhilGips, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Okay. Pero kayo ngayon, sir, puwede niyo namang reviewhin yung mga nakaraan na mga, ika nga, mga kontrata, projects, hindi lang po itong tungkol sa Davao but other government projects. Di ba wala kayong ganoong mandato na silipin, tingnan, baka napakadami na o halos lahat ng ating mga proyekto ay may problema?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Hindi po parte ng mandato pero kadalasan po kasi sa division namin we receive various requests po talaga when it comes to procurement data. Nire-request po ng mga iba't ibang agencies na pinaprovide po namin sa kanila.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: So ngayon po wala kayong planong maybe reviewin man lang?

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Sir, hindi po ninyo mandato. Kasi may mga incidents po tayo, sir, di po ba, na maraming ikang graft and corruption cases. Case in point, yung flood control po na yan. Na because hindi po ninyo, dahil hindi ninyo mandato, kaya hindi po ninyo na-check. Bakit kaya po magkusa na lang yung inyong departamento mismo? Dahil bagamat repository kayo, pwede nyo silipin.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: May, Your Honor, meron pong, I think na, proper agency na could address those. What I'm

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: pointing at is kayo mismo magkusa lang. Hindi po pwede dahil wala sa mandato ninyo to check yung mga hawak ninyong mga files. Basta pag dumating sa inyo, ilalagay nyo lang niya sa isang gilid. Ipa-file na lang ninyo hanggat sa walang humingi.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: It's electronically filed po. Nasa database lang po siya. Hindi naman po siya yung hard copy talaga, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Yeah, pero you cannot? You cannot go through? I mean, silipin man lang?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Not part of the division's function po kasi we have other po na duties that we are also fulfilling.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness, Presiding Officer. Maraming salamat po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator-Judge Irwin. Senator-Judge Lacson to avail of his first round. You may proceed, sir. You have two minutes when you're ready.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: I'm not asking any question, Mr. Presiding Officer, but this is a very short manifestation based on my observation.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: proceed, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: The way probably and probably some of the non-lawyers among the senator-judges, particularly my seatmate, Senator Lapid, understand the questions posited by the Defense Council is that the objective of the cross was to create an iota of doubt, no matter how technical and small, to create the impression that the threshold of establishing guilt is beyond reasonable doubt, which I believe is not the case in this impeachment trial, Mr. Presiding Officer. Hindi po ito, let me clarify and emphasize na hindi po ito prejudgment. Ang hangat ko lang po is baka pwede mag-adjust kayo ng inyong defense strategy. Kasi I can speak for myself, pagdating sa masyadong technical at yung impresyo na nagsisilip lang ng napakalit na butas, mukhang hindi po nagre-register. So marami na rin ko yung naipunto in the course of the trial na magaganda. Pero pag nag-resort tayo sa yung we're trying to observe, kasi we were talking between kami dalawa. Yan ang observation namin. Parang hindi masyadong re-register. Parang napakalilit na butas na masyadong technical, medyo hindi po tumatalab. Maraming salamat po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Noted, Senator Lacson. Thank you very much. Finally, Senator Judge Rafi Tulfo for his interjection.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You have two minutes, sir. You may proceed when you're ready.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Mr. Witness, merong 15 contracts ang GenCorp. Ano na sa record? Yes. nasa record ng PhilGEPS para sa mga small value procurements. Now, nabanggit ng 15, magkano yung per contract dun sa 15 ang value?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Per

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: contract, I'm not sure, Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: That is correct.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Each?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Each. So, meron pong 5,143,500 pesos and meron pong 6,277,500 pesos. Meron din po rito na 9,800,000, 8,400,000, and yung meron po rito 500,000, 500, 1,600 pesos, 400,414 pesos.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay, that's enough. So, lampas sa 2,000,000?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Yung apat po na nauna, lagpas po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Kasi under Republic Act No. 12009 o New Government Procurement Act, Amount involved shall not exceed 2 million. So may binagat ka 4 million. Ano po ang iba?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Correct po. Those are conducted through public bidding.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: So sumobra-sobra pa?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Pag public bidding po, if I remember it correct, above 2 million is allowed po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Ah, that is public bidding. Hindi ba yan sa small value procurement?

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Hindi po. Ang small value po, your honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay,

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: yung tinatanong kayo sa small value.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Ah, yung small value po, yung 500,000. 500, 1,600 pesos, 414,000. Wala namang pong lumagpas ng 2 million po sa 11 na small value.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Nalito ko sa tanong ko. It's okay. Now, sabi ni Presiding Officer, I think kung pwede, we have to resolve this right here right now, kung pwede. Kasi sa SAL-N ni VP Sara, which is a sworn document, she reiterated in that SAL-N, na she's part owner of GenCorp. On the other hand, sa SEC, wala siyang record na nagmamayari. So, sinong paniniwalaan natin dito? Sino nagsisinungaling? Or is it because yung SEC ay nagkaroon ng oversight? Or si VP Sara, she was being honest, kaya nilagay niya talagang she owns it? So, anong susundin natin dito, Mr. Presiding Officer?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Sir?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Psst!

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Tulog ka na. Joke.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Dilat yung mata ko. I'm sorry. Yes, Senator-Judge Raffi.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Kasi sabi ko

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: kanina, to repeat my question, sasali ni BP Sara, which is a sworn document, nakalagay doon na part-owner siya ng

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: GenCorp. Kasi sabi mo, wala sa SEC. And paulit-ulit natin napakinggan yan, sino paniniwalaan natin ngayon? Anong pagbabasehan natin ang ating paniniwala?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: 'Yun bang sa sinumpang salaysay ni VP Sara sa SALN niya na she's part owner of GenCorp, o 'yung sa SEC wala siyang pangalan doon?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: That

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: is up for the parties to prove and or disprove at the proper time, Your Honor. The prosecution presented two witnesses that made conflicting claims. I expect them to clarify this matter before they rest their case and when the time for the defense, the respondent rather. will present their evidence in chief. I expect them to address this issue as well. Paumanhin, hindi pa natin kayang sagutin ng deretso yan at hindi ko pa rin kayang sagutin ng deretso. Magdedepende yan sa ebidensya ipapresentan ng mga kabilang panig sa akmang panahon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: No other Senator-Judge registered to make interjections. Chair will now excuse Mr. Yes, Honorable Luistro.

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Very quick manifestation only. In relation

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: to what, counsel?

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: This

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: is just to correct. The transcript of records, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, please,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Counsel.

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Earlier, I said that the procurement law does not explicitly provide about conflict of interest. I stand corrected, Your Honor. As a matter of fact, the Honorable Senate President, Sherwin Gatchalian, is very much correct when he said that there must be disclosure of relationship of the merchant to any of the officials of the procuring entity, Your Honor. And I totally agree with the Honorable Senator Rafi Tulfo when he made mention, when he implied the three violations, Your Honor. Owning business, operating business, and conflict of interest, Your Honor. In fact, ito ho kung sa larong tong-it, three hits po ito. That is all, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Chair will exclude that last part. From the comment of the lead prosecutor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: We submit,

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roberto N. Batungbacal
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Attorney Ravi.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roberto N. Batungbacal
turns.text: We just want to put on record or remind the prosecution we defer to the ruling of this impeachment court not to make conclusions of law or conclusions of fact or to supplement the testimony of the witness, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The ruling was already made by the Chair.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Mr. Supena, tapos na po ang inyong pagtestigo. Maraming salamat po sa inyong oras at panahon at salamat po sa pagsagot sa mga katanungan na magkabilang partido, gayon din, ng mga miyembro ng hukumang ito. Maraming salamat po. Your excuse, sir.

turns.speaker: Rendell P. Sopeña
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Before we call on the next witness, whom you can situate already, the OSA, the Clerk of Court is directed to situate, Mr., rather, Police Major Sangalang.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly situate him to the witness stand.

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, please, we are yielding to the Head Prosecutor, the Honorable Ridon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: While you are doing that and while we are situating, Police Major Sangalang, Chair would like to place on record that we are in receipt of a letter from Mayor Sebastian Duterte of the City of Davao on even date, dated today.

So I presume, Honorable Ridon, after Police Major Sangalang, we will be presenting tomorrow, Mayor Sebastian Duterte.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: That is

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly turn on the mic of Honorable Ridon.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: That is correct, Your

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Okay, with respect to the other requests for subpoena, we will act on that before we adjourn today.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: Bago po isalang si Police Major Sangalang, we wanted to reiterate si Atty. Gary Samonte, hindi na po isasalang, yung pong PhilHealth witness.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Share hereby recalls the subpoena issued to Mr., what's his name again? Atty. Samonte. Mr. Samonte, as manifested and moved by the Council for the Panel of Prosecutors. So ordered.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: Your Honor, please. Bago po isalang si Mr. Sangalang, maybe we can break for lunch already so that the direct testimony can be continuous instead of breaking for lunch later.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Yes, Mr. Presiding Officer. Matanong ko lamang po at saka sa ating prosecution. Ano ang kinalaman nga pala ng Major Sangalang sa issue na ito? Marami po kasi kami nagtatanong ano ba kasama rin po ba ito sa unexplained wealth, hidden wealth ng ating vicepresidente. Can somebody tell me sa prosecution?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Allow the chair. Sa pagkakaunawa ko, pinapresento ang testigo nito para patotohanan ang pagmamayari, di o mano, ng ikalawang pangulo ng samotsaring mga armas na siguro ko ay bibigyan nila ng halaga. Sa pagsuma ng kanyang SAL-N ayon sa kanilang pre-trial brief.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Ito po ba ang mga armas na ito? Mga gold-plated or may mga diamond po ba ito?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Hindi ko po masasagot. Mga bala po ay

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: diamante.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Hindi ko po masasagot. Yung testigo lamang po ang makakasagot niyan kung sakasakali. We will hear the purpose for which this witness is being offered once the offer is made, Senator-Judge Irwin.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Maraming salamat po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Doon pa lang natin makikita kung katanggap-tanggap nga ba o hindi. At kung hindi katanggap-tanggap, the gentleman can make the appropriate motion at that time.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Maraming salamat po sa paliwanag na yan, Mr. Presiding Officer. Thank you po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Before

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: we pause on our lunch recess, can we place the witness under oath already, sir, that we at least are able to do that? Kindly stand up, Police Major Sangalang. Is it Sangalang or Sangalang?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Sangalang, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Sangalang. Okay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Please raise your right hand. You, Joericson Sangalang. Do swear that the evidence you shall give in the case now pending between the Philippines and Vice President Cyrus Jim Ramon Duterte shall be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. So help me God.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly sit down. Naunawaan niyo po inyong pinanumpaan ng Police Major Sangalang?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Opo, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Mag lunch break lang muna tayo. So kumain po kayo. May lugar yata kayo para kumain.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We shall resume upon the request of Senator-Judge Lacson at 12.30. And we shall take a lunch recess and our lunch break. When we resume, we shall listen to the direct examination of the witness by the counsel for the panel of prosecutors. The court is in recess.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Honorable Ridon,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: who will be presenting the witness? Kindly situate Police Major Sangalang to the witness stand.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Who will be presenting the witness, Honorable Ridon?

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. We are ready to proceed with direct examination of the witness. The prosecutor who will conduct the direct is Honorable Isabel Maria J. Zamora of the Lone District of San Juan City.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The Honorable Zamora is recognized on the part of the respondent.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honor, I am turning over to Carlo Joaquin P. Narvasa.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Attorney Narvasa, what's your nickname?

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: CJ, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: CJ.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Good afternoon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So, Attorney Zamora, the Honorable Zamora and Attorney Narvasa.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Nag-change costume ka ba o naka-jacket ka lang kanina?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Naka-jacket po ako kanina, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Ah, okay. Akala ko nag-change costume ka eh.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Parang nagbago eh.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Forgive me for that, Police Major Sangalang. Honorable Zamora, you may make your offer, ma'am, when you're ready.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honors. Good afternoon. We offer the testimony of Police Major Joericson Sangalang. First, to prove that the witness is a police major of the Philippine National Police assigned to the Firearms and Explosives Office as its Chief of the Records Section and is a member of the Firearms Classification Board. Two, to prove that the PNP Through the FEO, processes and approves applications for the issuance of licenses to qualified individuals and causes the registration of firearms in accordance with Republic Act No. 10591 and its implementing rules and regulations. 3. To prove that the respondent Vice President Sara Duterte Carpio and her husband, Atty. Mance Carpio, both possess licenses to own and possess firearms, LTOP. Type 5, and are classified as certified gun collectors. 4. To prove that the Vice President and her husband maintain a hobby in gun collecting by owning, possessing, and maintaining at least 50 firearms, which includes pistols, revolvers, rifles, and shotguns, with a total value of at least 7 million pesos. 5. To prove such other relevant allegations and to identify and authenticate relevant documents.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Comment on the part of Attorney CJ?

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. First, Your Honor, the defense registers its continuing objection to the introduction of testimony and documents in relation to Attorney Carpio. This is in relation to this Honorable Court's July 2026 ruling. However, Your Honor, we do not request the Honorable Court for any ruling today, but merely ask that our objection be noted.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Second, Your Honor, as to the fourth purpose, the witness would be incompetent to testify on any supposed value of the firearms as he is testifying as Chief of the Firearms and Explosives Office who has no expertise in appraisal. Still on the fourth purpose, Your Honor, we object also to the amount that the

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Prosecution has offered for the same reason as previously stated, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Any comment, Honorable Zamora?

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honor, as regards the first objection, the continuing objection as regards Attorney Manassas Manscarpio, the Honorable Presiding Officer has time and again ruled that the assets of Attorney Manscarpio should be included. In the deliberations before this Honorable Impeachment Court, considering that the assets of Atty. Man Scarpio form part or should be also stated in the Salen of the Vice President. This is in tune with the ruling of this Honorable Court as regards the Salen and the financial records of the Vice President and Atty. Man Scarpio. As regards The objection to the fourth offer that the witness is incompetent to testify because his functions do not include an appraisal or the appraisal of revolvers. He will be testifying based on the records of his office or the FEO as well as What is stated in the certification that he will be presenting before this honorable court in the same vein that the amount stated in the offer is the same amount that is stated in the certification that will be presented by the witness, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Just

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: a quick rebuttal, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Attorney CJ.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Your Honor, I just would like to clarify the record. This Honorable Court has only ruled on the first issue once, on the 20th of July, Your Honor, and not time and again. Second, Your Honor, I would like to thank the Honorable Zamora for her admission that the appraisal of any firearms are not the functions of the witness. So I'd like to thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Before we continue, earlier the Honorable Erwin Tulfo raised a question which I believe is more proper now after the witness, after rather the member of the panel of prosecutors has made her offer. Would the Honorable Tulfo or, yes, like to reiterate his earlier query, cum manifestation?

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Yes, Mr. Presiding Officer, kagaya po ng tanong ko kanina, ano po ang relevance ng magiging statement ni Major Sangalang dito sa pinag-uusapan natin tungkol po sa hidden wealth or unexplained wealth? Kaya nga po kanina, though it was sort of a, yung question ko po is sort of a joke na may diamante ba, may gold ba yung baril na yan that we have to tackle all the firearms. Kung sasabihin na napakaraming firearms, marami naman po mga Pilipino, marami din mga firearms. Marami din po mga kolektor na mga baril, mga businessman, mga ika nga officials na... Maraming baril. So, I don't see the relevance here, Mr. Presiding Officer. But, what's your decision?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: believe the Honorable Soto also intimated to the Presiding Officer his reservation with respect to this witness. Would Senator-Judge Soto care to elaborate?

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer. I was just asking our colleagues, the fellow Senator-Judges earlier that I think the offer that was going to be given and as given now and that Senator Turpo was asking earlier is if these were contained in the sal-in of the Vice President. Am I right, Mr. President?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I think that's the direction they are headed towards, Senator Soto.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The Honorable Zamora did not mention that in her offer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Well, I leave it up to you because I have been reviewing my Sal-N also and I do not see anything there that says guns.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: And you simply include it as part of personal property, I guess?

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Yes, I usually do that and I do that myself in the personal properties. So I leave the question to the court,

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Your

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The Honorable Zubiri was also expressing some sentiments earlier to the Presiding Officer. Will you kindly place it on record as well, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Juan Miguel “Migz” F. Zubiri
turns.text: Yes, Mr. President. Actually, while we were having lunch, we were discussing in the lounge the importance of this particular... With due respect to Congresswoman Zamora, we're friends and all, but we just want to make sure of the relevance of this particular evidence because Many of us are firearms owners here, if not all members of the Senate. We usually put it under personal effects and personal properties, Your Honor, Mr. President. So, I don't see there's any violation that I feel would happen if they do that, if the Vice President had done that. I don't think it's that much weight. We're looking for the bigger evidence that they want to present. If

turns.speaker: Sen. Juan Miguel “Migz” F. Zubiri
turns.text: any.

turns.speaker: Sen. Juan Miguel “Migz” F. Zubiri
turns.text: If any. Sabi nga ni Senator Lacson, yung malaking paputok maging kwitis. Saan na

turns.speaker: Sen. Juan Miguel “Migz” F. Zubiri
turns.text: yung malaking putok umabot sa atomic bomb kung meron? Yan ang gusto po natin malaman. With due respect, of course, to the prosecution. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator-Judge Allan Cayetano is recognized. On the subject matter, Senator-Judge Allan, yes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Just to clarify the pleasure of our colleagues. So first, so basically the question is if the Honorable Major will testify on anything major. Secondly, whether the guns constitute a smoking gun or seriously, given the time that both parties said we want to use judiciously para matapos kaagad yung trial in a fair manner, that we will come up with a verdict acceptable to our people. I joined them, Mr. Presiding Officer, Mr. Senate President, if yun yung question na kung major ba to minor. Ang konti ko lang reservation is kung sana magkasundo yung prosecution at defense if we disregard this. Kasi I don't want the judges be the one to tell them what they can present and not. Unless nga we rule it's irrelevant. So just with that, I joined them in the sentiment. Yung konting caution lang. But I hope, yun nga, we can find a way that both the prosecution and defense will agree on something. So that... Yung process lang nung how we dispense with this issue, Mr. Presiding Officer. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator Subiri.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Major Sangalang, you have a list of the firearms registered in the name of the Vice President and her spouse?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Counsel, Attorney CJ, are you willing to stipulate as to the list?

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: No, Your Honor. We have yet to receive any.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You haven't seen the list?

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: None, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: If I give you time to look at the list, would you be in a position to stipulate? I'm headed towards excluding this witness, counsel.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Hold

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: on, Honorable Zamora.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: To be quite candid, Your Honor, even if we were given time to peruse any list that the good Major will be presenting, we believe that this witness is irrelevant. Whatever he would state, it would be irrelevant. So we have the same reservations as the good senators.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Honorable Zamora, I hope you see where we're coming from. Even assuming he can put a price on the firearms that the spouses own at 7 million, that's well within the SAL-N she submitted of, I believe, 88 million as of the latest.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: And there is no requirement to declare the firearms as a separate category in the SAL-N. Yes, Honorable Zamora, can you respond?

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Actually,

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honor, if I may manifest, the guidelines for the SAL-N actually require a statement of the firearms. Under Section 34, it states there that personal property registered with the appropriate government agency such as but not limited to motor vehicles, boats, aircraft, and firearms shall be declared individually.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Your Honor, if I may

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: respond,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: kindly let her finish.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Sorry, apology, I thought you

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: were done.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honor, also as regards the certification, the list that was mentioned earlier, the Police Major Sangalang has the certification with the list of the firearms of the respondent as well as her husband.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The list of firearms.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: The list of firearms are with Police Major Sangalang and we believe that it was issued yesterday.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: How about the value of 7 million? What would be the basis of Major Sangalang in proving the value of the Firearms Council?

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honor, that is in the list as well.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: That he produced?

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: He will be presenting the list or the certification before this honorable court.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: And the values are stated there. And if questions will be propounded to the good gentleman, then he will be able to respond as to where the values are taken.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Major Sangalang, you are in a position to state the amount or the value of each firearm?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. It is listed in our certification.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: On the basis of what? Acquisition value or fair market value?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: It's on our... Market Survey, as of the current price, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: What if the gun was given to her?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: If the gun was given to her, how would the value be relevant? By way of acquisition, sir,

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: By way of acquisition, sir, it will be a donation, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So, hindi kailangan isama?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Naka-check na po namin yung records niya and wala naman pong donation, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Your witness, counsel, but may I remind you to kindly abbreviate it because as most of the senator-judges have mentioned, we find this witness not as convincing with respect to ill-gotten wealth as would be others, given at only the small value of this.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: but also given that as stated by Senator-Judge Soto, these are not separately listed in other declarations of SAL-N by other officials. Yes, Attorney CJ.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. If I may just comment on the explanation of the Honorable Zamora. Your Honor, what she quoted was the 2025 CSC rules, which... do not have application to the silence of the Vice President as those will be applicable only for submissions beginning 2026, Your Honor. And also as regards the market value that the witness had already said, that again is irrelevant because what is pertinent, Your Honor, is the acquisition cost. So from the very beginning, The witness's testimony has proven to be no value.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: With all due respect, of course.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Are you willing to stipulate with respect to the position of Police Major Sangalang?

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Yes,

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: And that he will be testifying as to the firearms that are licensed to the Vice President and her spouse based on their records?

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So that foregoes with offers number 1 and 2.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Honorable Zamora, you may proceed with your direct examination. In relation to offers 3 and 4. If you may.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed, ma'am. And again, let's try to abbreviate the proceedings insofar as this witness is concerned. Let's try to finish them today. You may proceed, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honors, we will abbreviate our questions.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed to offer number 3 and 4 and so on.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Mr. Witness, good afternoon. Mag-focus po tayo sa LTOP.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Ano pong iba't-ibang uri ng LTOP? Kung meron man.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Relevance.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I'll allow it, counsel. I know where she said that. She's trying to abbreviate the proceedings in accordance with the court's instruction. Please answer, Major Sangalang.

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Meron po tayong dalawang classification ng LTAF. Yun po ay ang individual and juridical. Under the individual, meron po tayong limang types, Type 1 to 5. Sa Type 1 po ay maaari po siyang magkaroon ng hanggang dalawang firearms.

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Sa Type 2, hanggang 5. Sa Type 3, hanggang 10. Sa Type 4, hanggang 15. At sa Type 5 po ay more than 15 firearms.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Base po sa records ng PNPFEO, ano po ang uri ng license na na-issue kay Vice President Sara?

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. No testimony has yet been made.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Your Honor, we're trying to abbreviate the proceedings.

turns.speaker: Atty. Carlo Joaquin T. Narvasa
turns.text: We withdraw the objection, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, with

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: your indulgence,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Attorney

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: CJ. Please, please continue, Honorable Zamora.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Again, Mr. Witness, base po sa record ng PNP-FEO, anong uri ng lisensya po kung meron man ang na-issue kay Vice President Sara?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Meron po siyang LTOP Type 5 po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: At ano naman pong uri ng lisensya ang na-issue ng PNP-FEO kay Vice President Sara?

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Atty. Man Scarpio.

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: LTOP Type 5 din po ma'am.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Okay, maraming salamat.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Puntahan lang natin yung LTOP Type 5. Compared with other LTOP Type 1, Type 4, what special requirement is sought from a Type 5 licensee kung meron ma'am?

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Para po sa mga LTAP holder ng Type 3, Type 4 to Type 5 po, they are required to have a physical inspection of their vault. Kailangan po meron po talaga silang vault and nire-require po na i-inspect po ito.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Okay, thank you po. Puntahan po natin ang firearms ni Respondent Vice President Sara at ng kanyang asawa.

turns.speaker: Rep. Ysabel Maria J. Zamora
turns.text: Batay po sa... Batay po sa records ng inyong tanggapan, ilang pong baril ang nakarehistro sa pangalan ni Vice President Sara.

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
turns.text: Can

turns.speaker: Police Major Joericson H. Sangalang
